rules.title: core.fsmonitor runs an external command
rules.explanation: Git invokes core.fsmonitor while refreshing the index, which happens during ordinary commands such as git status and git diff. Coding agents run those commands automatically when they open a project, so a command placed here executes on your machine without any prompt. This is the primary vector described in the GitSpawn research and in CVE-2026-45033.
rules.remediation: Remove the key, or run git with -c core.fsmonitor=false until you have reviewed it.

rules.title: core.sshCommand replaces the ssh binary
rules.explanation: Any fetch, pull or push over ssh runs this command instead of ssh.
rules.remediation: Remove the key unless you deliberately set it yourself.

rules.title: core.gitProxy runs an external command for git:// connections
rules.explanation: The configured program is executed instead of a direct connection.
rules.remediation: Remove the key unless your network genuinely requires a proxy command.

rules.title: core.pager points at an unusual command
rules.explanation: The pager runs whenever git prints paged output such as log, diff or show.
rules.remediation: Set it to a known pager (less, delta, bat) or remove it.

rules.title: core.editor points at an unusual command
rules.explanation: The editor runs on commit, rebase and tag operations.
rules.remediation: Set it to a known editor or remove it.

rules.title: sequence.editor points at an unusual command
rules.explanation: This command runs during an interactive rebase.
rules.remediation: Set it to a known editor or remove it.

rules.title: core.hooksPath redirects hooks to a non-default directory
rules.explanation: Git normally runs hooks from .git/hooks. An override can point at a directory shipped inside the repository, so its scripts run on ordinary git operations while .git/hooks looks untouched.
rules.remediation: Inspect the target directory before running any git command in this repository.

rules.title: include / includeIf loads configuration from another file
rules.explanation: Included files can add any of the keys on this list later, which keeps the dangerous value out of the file you inspect.
rules.remediation: Open the included file and check it against this same list. A shared ~/.gitconfig you created yourself is normal.

rules.title: diff.external runs an external diff program
rules.explanation: Git runs this program for every diff, including the diffs coding agents generate to read your changes.
rules.remediation: Remove the key unless you configured the tool yourself.

rules.title: credential.helper runs a program that receives your credentials
rules.explanation: A credential helper is executed by git and is handed the host and username it is asked about. A repository-local helper can both execute code and capture tokens.
rules.remediation: Credential helpers belong in your global config, not in a repository. Remove it here.

rules.title: Git alias executes a shell command
rules.explanation: An alias value starting with ! is run through the shell. Aliases defined inside a repository run as soon as someone uses that alias name.
rules.remediation: Read the command. Aliases that shell out do not belong in a repository-local config.

rules.title: Filter driver runs a command on checkout or commit
rules.explanation: Filter drivers referenced from .gitattributes run automatically whenever matching files are checked out or staged. git-lfs uses this legitimately; anything else deserves a look.
rules.remediation: Check .gitattributes to see which files trigger this driver, and read the command.

rules.title: diff textconv runs a command to render a file as text
rules.explanation: Referenced from .gitattributes and executed whenever git diffs a matching file.

rules.title: Custom merge driver runs a command during a merge
rules.explanation: Executed by git when merging files that .gitattributes assigns to this driver.

rules.title: Merge/diff tool command defined in the repository
rules.explanation: Runs when someone starts git mergetool or git difftool.
rules.remediation: Read the command before using those subcommands.

rules.title: uploadpack.packObjectsHook runs a command when the repository is fetched from
rules.explanation: Executed on the serving side of a fetch or clone.
rules.remediation: Remove the key unless you run this repository as a server and set it yourself.

rules.title: A git transport protocol is re-enabled for this repository
rules.explanation: Git disables the ext:: and other helper transports by default because they let a URL name a command to run. Setting protocol.allow (or protocol.<name>.allow) back to 'always' re-enables that, and a submodule or remote URL is then enough to execute something.
rules.remediation: Remove the key. If a project genuinely needs a non-default transport, allow it per command, not in the repository's own config.

rules.title: Remote URL uses a transport that executes a command
rules.explanation: A URL beginning with ext:: passes the rest of the line to a shell as the transport helper. Fetching, cloning or initialising a submodule with such a URL runs that command.
rules.remediation: Do not fetch this remote or initialise this submodule. Read the URL first.

structural.title: Bare git repository found inside the project tree
structural.explanation: Git discovers bare repositories while walking directories and applies their configuration, including keys that execute commands. This is the exact mechanism of CVE-2026-45033 (GitHub Copilot CLI, CVSS 8.5). A bare repository that ships inside a project is almost never legitimate.
structural.remediation: Do not open this project with a coding agent until you have inspected the directory. Setting safe.bareRepository=explicit in your global git config stops git from picking up bare repositories automatically.

structural.title: Nested .git directory below the project root
structural.explanation: A .git directory that is not the project's own repository arrived as content, for example through a zip file, a shared drive or a sync folder. Its config is read by git and by coding agents that gather context from it. Submodules are the legitimate exception.
structural.remediation: Check whether this is a registered submodule (.gitmodules). If it is not, treat it as untrusted and inspect its config.

structural.title: Active hook script present in .git/hooks
structural.explanation: A freshly cloned repository only contains .sample files. An active hook runs automatically on ordinary git operations such as commit, checkout and merge.
structural.remediation: Read the script. If you did not create it, remove it before running git commands here.

structural.title: Hooks directory managed by a known hook manager
structural.explanation: core.hooksPath points at a conventional, repository-managed hooks directory (husky, lefthook or the .githooks convention). This is normal in many projects. GuardSkill read the scripts and found nothing that fetches code or reaches into a temporary location — but these scripts do run on ordinary git operations, so the evidence line lists them.
structural.remediation: No action needed if you expect this project to use managed hooks. The listed scripts are what will run.

structural.title: Hook script installed by a known hook manager
structural.explanation: An active hook in .git/hooks carries the marker of a known hook manager. This is how husky, lefthook and pre-commit install themselves.
structural.remediation: No action needed if you installed that tool.

structural.title: Hook script downloads or decodes code before running it
structural.explanation: A git hook that pipes a download into a shell, decodes base64, or evaluates a command substitution is doing something a build hook has no reason to do. Hooks run automatically on ordinary git operations.
structural.remediation: Do not run any git command in this repository until you have read the script.

structural.title: .gitmodules declares a submodule whose URL executes a command
structural.explanation: A submodule URL beginning with ext:: hands the rest of the line to a shell when the submodule is initialised. Coding agents and IDEs initialise submodules automatically in some configurations.
structural.remediation: Do not run git submodule update in this repository until you have read .gitmodules.

structural.title: Hook script runs something from a temporary or hidden location
structural.explanation: core.hooksPath points at a conventionally named directory (.husky, .githooks), which is normal, but one of its scripts references a temporary or hidden path. Build hooks run project tooling from the project; they have no reason to reach into /tmp, /var/tmp or a hidden cache directory.
structural.remediation: Read the script before running any git command in this repository.
